messages.content: 從一顆距離地球4光年的恆星發出的光需要多少時間才能抵達地球？

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.

message.reasoning: We need to compute light travel time from a star 4 light-years away. Light travels at speed of light. The distance is 4 light-years. So time = distance / speed? But distance in light-years already accounts for speed of light: 1 light-year is distance light travels in one year. So 4 light-years means 4 years. So answer: 4 years. But we can also use function to compute. The function expects distance_in_light_years and speed_of_light optional. We can call with distance=4. It will compute time in seconds? Let's check function signature: It says "Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another." Input: distance_in_light_years: number, speed_of_light?: number. Output: any. Likely returns time in seconds or maybe years. But we can compute manually: 4 light-years = 4 years. So answer: 4 years. Provide explanation. Use function? The user asked: "從一顆距離地球4光年的恆星發出的光需要多少時間才能抵達地球？" They want time. So answer: 4 years. We can also show calculation: 1 light-year = 9.461e15 meters. Speed of light ~ 299792458 m/s. So time = distance / speed. But easier: 4 years. Provide answer in years. Also mention seconds: 4 * (365.25*24*3600) ≈ 126,230,400 seconds? Wait 1 year ~ 31,557,600 seconds. So 4 years ~ 126,230,400 seconds. Actually 31,557,600 * 4 = 126,230,400. So answer: 4 years (~126 million seconds). Provide explanation. Use function? We can call function to confirm.
